title: Ask Archipelago: synthesis and probe plans (Feb 2026)
body:
Purpose and framing:
- Quick synthesis of customer asks gathered Jan–Feb 2026 from EMEA pilot customers, two enterprise pilots (FinServ-X, HealthCo), and ~35 inbound support threads.
- Use "archipelago" metaphor: many small, related asks scattered across product areas; goal = identify high-ROI small probes (islands we can visit quickly) + 2 medium experiments to scope into PM backlog.

Notes to self / tone: choppy, intentionally half-baked. This is a field-driven brainstorming doc for partner with Product/Eng to convert to concrete tickets.

Raw microthemes (top-of-mind clusters)
1) Latency unpredictability on bursty routes
   - Quote: "One minute it's 80ms, next minute it's 600ms for the same endpoint" (FinServ-X CS contact).
   - Customer pain: user-facing features degrade; hard to trust SLAs for demos.

2) Token billing surprises for cached/streamed responses
   - Customers see cost spikes when we change model variant or when streaming chunks re-send prefixes.
   - Quote: "We suddenly got billed 3x monthly for a feature we didn't change."

3) Embedding drift & versioning clarity
   - Customers doing similarity search notice drift after model refresh. Need stable version pins and a migration path.

4) Canary / rollout visibility and rollback ergonomics
   - Platform teams want a clearer timeline + ability to test rollback on a subset of traffic without prod config gymnastics.

5) Private deployment onboarding friction
   - Long checklist, unclear prerequisites for KMS and network ACLs. Pilot customers ask for a one-click preflight.

Prioritized micro-probes (fast experiments / quick-fix proposals)
- Probe A: latency-runbook flag (owner: Liam) — small runtime change to add a per-route latency guardrail that caps batching dynamically above X ms for the last N requests.
  - Hypothesis: adaptive cap will flatten tail latency for bursty workloads and reduce customer complaints by 60% on affected routes.
  - Effort: small (2 sprint-days infra + 2 QA days).
  - Measurement: tail p95/p99 by route (compare last 14d baseline).
  - Risk: may reduce throughput; need throttling metrics.

- Probe B: streaming-cost-audit + SDK patch (owner: Priya) — run a one-week audit of streaming sessions to detect duplicated prefix tokens, then ship SDK that avoids re-sending cached prefix on reconnects.
  - Hypothesis: reduce unexpected charge incidents by 40% for customers using streaming.
  - Effort: medium (backend audit 3d, SDK change 3d, docs 1d).
  - Measurement: incidents tagged "billing-surprise" in CS pipeline + per-customer token spend delta.

- Probe C: embedding-pin pilot (owner: Daniel) — add explicit embedding-version header and a "pin" flag in the embeddings API; show a migration assistant in Console to diff old vs new embeddings for a sample corpus.
  - Hypothesis: clear pins reduce churn and support load for similarity regressions.
  - Effort: medium (API + Console UI prototype, 2 sprints).

- Probe D: private-deploy preflight checklist generator (owner: Sofia) — interactive checklist that collects customer env details and outputs a ready-made ACL/KMS config and a progress-estimate PDF.
  - Hypothesis: reduces onboarding time/calls by ~30% and increases Private POC conversion.
  - Effort: small (1 sprint dev + 1 doc).

Mapping micro-probes to tickets / who to pull in
- Latency-runbook flag -> ENG: serving-runtime + SRE review (JIRA: ENG-8420). Pull: Rohan (runtime), Mei (SRE).
- Streaming audit -> SDK + billing infra (billing lead: Arjun). Open ticket: CS-1123 for incident tracking.
- Embedding pin -> product-hosted-api + applied-ml (owner: Katerina).
- Preflight checklist -> solutions-engineering + console-and-tooling (owner: Sofia).

Customer vignettes (short)
- FinServ-X: revenue demo failed during live demo because a canary change bumped latency; asked for per-route traffic pin and a rollback plan. Mental model: enterprise customers want predictable runway for demos; even intermittent tail blips break their trust.
- HealthCo: embedding mismatch after model swap led to duplicate patient matches. They want a way to "freeze" embeddings for critical indices.
- Mid-market SaaS (N=6): billing spike after switching to new streaming SDK; they do not have dev resources to dig in; expect CS to act as advisor.

Decision criteria for which probes to run now
- Quick wins (<=1 sprint) with clear metric we can measure within 2 weeks -> prioritize.
- High-customer-impact + low-engineering-effort -> prioritize.
- Regulatory / compliance blockers -> escalate to CC (security/compliance).

Proposed short-run roadmap (6 weeks)
- Week 0–1: finalize probe scope + get ENG/ML signoff. Create 4 JIRA tickets with owners and acceptance criteria.
- Week 2–3: run Probe A + Probe B (parallel). Monitor p99 and billing incidents.
- Week 4: iterate on Probe B SDK feedback; cook up a customer-facing summary for affected customers.
- Week 5–6: start Probe C (embedding pin) as a staged rollout with two pilot customers (HealthCo + one mid-market).

Measurement plan (simple)
- Primary metrics: p95/p99 latency by route, number of "billing-surprise" incidents tagged in CS, number of private POCs that complete onboarding within SLA.
- Secondary: CS NPS delta for pilot customers, number of support escalations for embedding drift.

Open questions / trade-offs (for Product + Eng meeting)
- How do we balance latency guardrails vs throughput SLOs? If we cap batching during tails, throughput will drop—do we prefer predictable latency at cost of capacity?
- Is embedding pinning a long-term UX (version management) problem or a stop-gap? If we offer pinning, we need migration tools and a billing model for storing multiple embedding sets.
- For streaming-cost fixes, do we change server behavior or only patch SDKs? Customers may be on older SDKs; server-side mitigation may be needed.

Suggested immediate next actions (owner tags)
- @Liam: write short RFC for latency-runbook flag, include p99 baseline (due 2026-02-17).
- @Priya: run streaming session query and produce sample of 10 affected customers (due 2026-02-20).
- @Daniel: draft API sketch for embedding pin header and sample migration flow (due 2026-02-24).
- @Sofia: prototype simple preflight template (Google doc + checklist) and test with Solutions Eng next week (due 2026-02-21).

Low-effort communications to reduce churn now
- CS templated explanation for billing spikes: what to look for, how to request a token audit.
- Short "how pinning works" FAQ to send to customers worried about embedding refreshes.
- Slack shortcut for field reps: /cs-quick-report that auto-tags incidents as "billing-surprise" or "latency-tail" for tracking.

Risks and mitigation
- Risk: engineering capacity overcommit -> mitigation: triage with PM to T-shirt-size each probe; drop lowest ROI.
- Risk: customers on old SDKs won't see fixes -> mitigation: server-side rate-limiting protections plus outreach to top 10 customers.

Appendix: raw quotes (anonymized)
- "Billing doubled overnight, we didn't change anything on our side."
- "We can't demo because the latency spikes once per 30 minutes, and our users notice."
- "Embedding results looked totally different after the update. We had to revert."

End notes / meta
- This doc intentionally mixes evidence + proposals. Use it as input for a 30-min sync with PM + Eng leads.
- If we get buy-in, convert probes into scoped sprint tasks with clear acceptance criteria and add to CS playbook.

-- Maya (notes)
